head: The hydroponics drum is now a pressure torus.
text: The old drum was a slab with flat end walls 28 m tall, which could not hold air. It is now a round-cornered torus four rack decks deep, carried on lattice webs and access tubes, with the greenhouse glazing in two rim bands and in bays on the end walls.

head: The reception pavilions are glazed tubes.
text: The two halls on the wheel's forward wall were rows of flat boxes. Each is now one curved pressure tube with domed ends, glazed forward and overhead, with a deck, lamps and planters inside.

head: The shuttle bay is an open hangar.
text: The pressurised box under the hull became an unpressurised barrel hangar with clamshell doors. One shuttle hangs below on the cradle, the second sits inside, and the opening is now wide enough for the wings.

head: The radiators are built from panels.
text: Both sets of swept fins were solid slabs. They are now rows of panels in a frame of ribs and an edge boom, fed by manifolds at the root and held flat by stay rods. Their outlines and areas are unchanged.

head: The wheel and the science ring are real hulls.
text: Each is one continuous pressure hull with an arched roof, bumper plates on the rim, windows with mullions, round elevator lobbies on the spokes and crossed stay rods. The wheel carries the ship's name and registry on its rim.

head: Observatory, flywheel and booms were rebuilt.
text: The dome is clear glass on a ribbed frame with a furnished deck inside, and its Whipple shutters are tapered gores that fold in a Z beside the collar. The flywheel is a levitated rim rotor in a vacuum torus on tube struts, and the sensor booms are lattice masts.
